notes: Identity: supplied canonical text has the matching title Revisiting the decoy effect: Replication and extension of Ariely and Wallsten (1995) and Connolly, Reb, and Kausel (2013), and authors Qinyu Xiao, Shiyuan Zeng, Gilad Feldman (p. 1). It identifies itself as an accepted final preprint, in press at Comprehensive Results in Social Psychology, accepted January 8, 2021, and reports completed methods/results plus supplementary materials. It is a primary completed report, not an abstract or preregistration alone. The supplied reference DOI is not printed in this text, so DOI identity cannot be independently confirmed from the permitted source. The reference year is 2020 whereas this accepted preprint is dated 2021. No PDF was supplied; no acquisition or rendering performed. Both assigned inputs identify Study 2 with exactly the same neutral description and p.18 locator; neither names Control versus Regret-Salient or baseline versus between-condition test. Printed manuscript p.18 concerns Study 1 instructions, not Study 2 results. No distinct target can be assigned to either audit_id. H1 exact binomial candidates compare target choice against .5, not a separately sampled no-decoy condition: Control analytic participants n=337, Cohen’s h=0.29, p<.001 (pp.35–37); Regret-Salient n=326, h=0.14, p=.017 (pp.35–37). The extension condition Low-Reversibility has n=327, h=0.17, p=.003 (p.36). H2 Control versus Regret-Salient Fisher exact test has printed χ2(1)=3.74, p=.057, φ=0.075 (p.38), a different metric/test from the within-condition Cohen’s h values. Do not pair its p with h. Model-specific candidate N for H2 is 337+326=663 mutually exclusive participants, corroborated by the explicit comparison on pp.46–47; no row-specific N is selected. Recruitment/final cohort N=1001 is not any one of these critical analytic samples. The main analyses exclude 52 participants under preregistered criteria and additionally remove decoy choosers (Control 2, Regret-Salient 5, Low-Reversibility 4). Supplementary full-sample results are alternative analyses, not substituted for main post-exclusion results. Printed candidates are retained here without metric conversion. Reported success is the explicit Study 2 overall verdict, mapped from partly successful to mixed; it does not disambiguate individual tests.
